text: (Places picture). Scene 15 Dorian’s Soul
speaker: C2

text: You have never looked more charming than you do tonight Dorian. You remind me of the day I saw you first. I wish you would tell me your secret. To get back my youth I would do anything in the world, except take exercise, get up early, or be respectable.
speaker: Lord Henery

text: I have changed Harry. I have done too many dreadful things in my life. I am not going to do any more. I began my good actions yesterday.
speaker: Dorian

text: Where were you yesterday?
speaker: Lord Henery

text: In the country.
speaker: Dorian

text: My dear boy anybody can be good in the country. There are no temptations the the country (To audience) He listened with an amused smile as Dorian tried to describe his transformation for a full twenty minutes.
speaker: Lord Henery

text: He was bored within seconds.
speaker: C2

text: (with clock face) Tick tock
speaker: Ensemble

text: Hetty is not one of our own class, of course. But I really loved her. I am quite sure that I loved her. All during this wonderful May I have ridden down to see her every week. Yesterday she met me in a little orchard. We were to have gone away together this morning at dawn. Suddenly I determined to leave her as flowerlike as I had found her.
speaker: Dorian

text: I should think the novelty of the emotion must have given you a thrill of real pleasure. So you broke this girl’s heart?
speaker: Lord Henery

text: Harry, you are horrible! Hetty's heart is not broken. Of course, she cried. But there is no disgrace upon her. She is unharmed.
speaker: Dorian

text: Do you think this girl will ever be content with anyone of her own rank now? From a moral point of view, I cannot say that I think much of your great renunciation. She will despise any husband and be wretched. And you bask in the glow of your goodness.
speaker: Lord Henery

text: Oh Harry! You mock at everything. I am sorry I told you now. Don't tell me that the first bit of self-sacrifice I have ever shown, is really a sort of sin.
speaker: Dorian

text: Oh you have saved her from society’s gossips but when have you or I cared about wagging tongues my dear Dorian? Whether you are good or bad society must have their bones to chew on.
speaker: Lord Henery

text: And society had been dining well of late.
speaker: C2

text: with a sumptuous feast,
speaker: C8

text: a never ending banquet
speaker: C4

text: of tasty morsels to pick over and embellish.
speaker: C5

text: (become characters)
speaker: C5/6/7/8

text: And what of Alan Campbell’s suicide?
speaker: C6

text: Wasn’t he once a close intimate of Dorian Gray?
speaker: C5

text: How many more young men will suffer from that man’s attentions?
speaker: C8

text: What of Basil Halward’s disappearance?
speaker: C5

text: Six weeks and no news. I hear Scotland Yard still insist that the man who boarded the midnight train on the ninth of November was poor Basil.
speaker: C6

text: The French police insist he never arrived in Paris at all.
speaker: C8

text: Have you heard that Victoria Wotton ran off with a pianist?
speaker: C5

text: I doubt Lord Henry has even noticed.
speaker: C6

text: They will learn that Dorian Gray has changed.
speaker: Dorian

text: (Lord H laughs) How can we be friends if you don’t believe I’ve changed?
speaker: Dorian

text: You cannot change in my eyes, and you and I will always be friends.
speaker: Lord Henery

text: Yet you poisoned me with a book. Harry, promise me that you will never lend that book to anyone. It does harm.
speaker: Dorian

text: Don’t moralise Dorian. You and I are what we are, and will be what we will be. The books that the world calls immoral are books that show the world its own shame.
speaker: Lord Henery

text: You are wrong Harry but I am too tired to argue.
speaker: Dorian

text: I will see you at the club for luncheon tomorrow Dorian. A good night’s sleep will help you to abandon these odd notions of goodness. (He exits)
speaker: Lord Henery

text: He could not rest after Lord Henry left.
speaker: C2

text: A new life! That was what he wanted.
speaker: C8

text: Surely he had begun it already. He had spared Hetty.
speaker: C4

text: He would never again tempt innocence. He would be good.
speaker: C5

text: He thought of the portrait that carried all his sins
speaker: C6

text: Perhaps the signs of evil had already gone away.
speaker: C8

text: He took the lamp from the table and crept upstairs. Yes, he would be good, and the hideous thing that he had hidden away would no longer be a terror to him.
speaker: Dorian

text: He dragged the purple hanging from the portrait.
speaker: C8

text: A cry of pain broke from him.
speaker: C2

text: The painting had changed
speaker: C5

text: But his wish had been perverted
speaker: C4

text: The mouth was more twisted.
speaker: C5

text: The eyes more cunning
speaker: C6

text: The thing was still loathsome.
speaker: C8

text: More loathsome than before.
speaker: All

text: Had there been nothing more in his renunciation than Vanity? Curiosity? Hypocrisy?
speaker: Dorian

text: There must be something more to his one good deed.
speaker: C8

text: His noble sacrifice.
speaker: C2

text: There had been nothing more.
speaker: All

text: Through vanity he had spared her.
speaker: C2

text: In hypocrisy he had worn the mask of goodness.
speaker: C4

text: For curiosity's sake he had tried the denial of self.
speaker: C5

text: He recognised that now
speaker: C6

text: His soul was base, evil, corrupted
speaker: All

text: And here was that soul for all to see
speaker: C4

text: The portrait declared to the world
speaker: C8

text: Taunting him
speaker: C2

text: Mocking him
speaker: C6

text: Here is Dorian Gray
speaker: All

text: No more!
speaker: Dorian

text: No more! He would destroy it.
speaker: All

text: He looked round and saw the knife that had stabbed Basil Hallward.
speaker: Dorian

text: As it had killed the painter, so it would kill the painter's work, and all that it had meant.
speaker: C4

text: It would kill the past.
speaker: C5

text: He would be free.
speaker: All

text: It would kill this monstrous soul-life.
speaker: C6

text: He would be at peace.
speaker: All

text: He seized it, and with a wild howl stabbed the vile travesty.
speaker: Dorian

text: A cry (Picture screams)
speaker: C5

text: Dorian and picture begin to revolve very slowly.
speaker: Stage

text: A soul wrenching cry.
speaker: All

text: DORIAN and Picture scream and keep screaming
speaker: Stage

text: A cry, so horrible in its agony, that it brought frightened servants from their rooms. (Ensemble in nightcaps peer out from entrance)
speaker: C8

text: turned Lord Henry back from the road
speaker: C2

text: Dorian is now in the Picture and stops screaming. The Old Dorian is now real and continues screaming as he falls to the floor
speaker: Stage

text: drew sobs from Old Mrs.Leaf
speaker: C5

text: Turned Francis pale as death.
speaker: C4

text: They climbed to the attic door.
speaker: Lord Henery

text: Silence
speaker: All

text: They knocked
speaker: C5

text: but there was no reply.
speaker: All

text: They called out. Others call out
speaker: C6

text: Everything was still.
speaker: All

text: Lord Henry entered and was faced with Dorian Gray. Painted in all the wonder of his exquisite youth and beauty.
speaker: Lord Henery

text: Lying on the floor was a dead man
speaker: C4

text: with a knife in his heart.
speaker: C8

text: He was withered,
speaker: C4

text: wrinkled,
speaker: C5

text: and loathsome of visage.
speaker: All

text: They examined his rings and finally knew…
speaker: Lord Henery

text: The distorted figure with evil etched in every line
speaker: C6

text: All was Dorian Gray.
speaker: All

text: THE END
speaker: Stage
